newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar's fate tied to U.S. assets, again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar's fate tied to U.S. assets, again.

text.p: The dollar's trading action overnight is likely to be the pivotal point for the U.S. currency's outlook through yearend, technical analysts said.
Again, the dollar's fate remains tied to investors' sentiment about U.S. assets, mainly stocks, they noted.
"There is an important support level on dollar/mark at 1.5350," said I.D.E.A. analyst Ben Morden. "It's pretty clear we've got to hold that line."
Analysts agreed the dollar must preserve key support in the 1.5340/50 area to avoid a serious setback that would lead straight to the next strong support level at 1.5290 marks.
However, in thinning trading volume ahead of the Christmas holiday, the dollar/mark upside appears capped at 1.5495/00, they added.
The dollar/yen outlook remains brighter since the 112.55 level -- or the 62-percent retracement of the upward move to the recent high at 113.70 -- held under fire on Wednesday.
"I'm a dollar bull, but it's just tough," Morden said. "We are at a pivotal juncture. The rest of December may be determined by the overnight price action."
A weak dollar would give nervous global investors only one more reason to divest U.S. assets through the yearend.
Dollar/Swiss, a good indicator of overall trend, tested near-term support at 1.3100 but held -- a mildly encouraging signal, analysts said.
Morden put the next support level on dollar/Swiss at 1.3060 but warned, if that were to give way, "it would not look good, and we would be looking at 1.30."

Analysts have cited concern over a sharp correction in U.S. equities as the main reason for dollar volatility since Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan cautioned about assets' overvaluation in a speech a week ago.
